title: Fine-grained page reclamation and eviction-window scheduler with kernel-aware batching
author: Marisa Chen
description: Context: In production we observed recurring tail memory amplification in the KV cache under mixed short/long-query workloads. Root cause analysis showed that fragmentation spikes and slow background reclamation delayed page reuse, which in turn forced synchronous spills and scheduler backpressure. This PR introduces an "epochal garbage sweeper" (a lightweight snapshot-driven reclaim path) plus a time-windowed eviction scheduler that coordinates kernel-aware batching decisions to reduce synchronous spill frequency and shorten tail latency. Changes: 1) Introduce kv::epochal_sweeper - periodic lightweight snapshot of hot/live page ranges with incremental compaction hooks to avoid long stop-the-world passes. 2) Add eviction-window scheduler that groups eviction candidates into bounded windows (by residency age and fragmentation_score) and applies soft thresholds to avoid abrupt spill waves. 3) Expose a fragmentation_score metric (0..1) derived from hole density and largest-free-run per region; scheduler uses this score to tune eviction aggressiveness. 4) Kernel-aware batching hints: when eviction-window is active we annotate outgoing inference batches so the runtime kernel selector prefers small-seq low-overhead kernels for affected hosts, improving throughput under memory-pressure. 5) Spillback backpressure: soft spill into host memory is now rate-limited with a token-bucket shaped by the eviction-window to stabilize latency. 6) Add telemetry: kv.fragmentation_score, kv.eviction_window_active, kv.sweeper_cycles, kv.soft_spill_rate. Motivation: reduce P99 generation latency and reduce synchronous GPU-to-host spill events that cost both time and GPU memory bandwidth. Checklist: - [x] design doc + diagrams in RFC - [x] unit tests for new algorithms - [x] integration tests on canary cluster - [x] perf microbenchmarks and regression gating - [x] console metrics and dashboard tile - [x] migration path and rollback plan (config flags) Backwards compatibility: all features gated behind runtime flags and env vars; default behavior unchanged. Rollout: staged canary (10% of dedicated capacity) -> 50% -> full. Observed improvements in microbenchmarks: P99 latency -18% on mixed workload, average token throughput +6%, synchronous spill events reduced by ~62% in synthetic hotspot tests. See linked linear tasks for details and evaluation harness runs. Migration and ops notes: operators can toggle KV_SWEEPER_ENABLED and EVICTION_WINDOW_MS; default windows set to conservative values for release. If issues observed operators can set EVICTION_WINDOW_MS=0 to disable scheduler and revert to previous evictor. Related work: builds on prior compaction efforts but differs by avoiding long compaction passes via epochal snapshots and by coordinating with kernel selection.

review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Nice approach. Can you clarify how epochal_sweeper avoids rereading large regions? Concerned about IO cost on cold starts.

Marisa Chen: The sweeper keeps weak references to hot ranges and uses a bloom hint to skip mostly-empty regions; cold-start IO is limited by a 1s rate cap. Added comments and tests (see commit e1b5f3a).
Priya Nair: Request change - make fragmentation_score stable across short windows to avoid thrashing. Suggest exponential smoothing.
Marisa Chen: Implemented exponential smoothing with configurable alpha (default 0.2). Added unit tests to validate stability.
Ethan Zhao: Verified metrics surface in console and added dashboard tile. Observed improved stability in staging. Approved after green CI.
CI Bot: perf checks show P99 -18% for mixed_workload_repro; baseline attached.
release_notes: Introduce epochal sweeper and eviction-window scheduler to reduce KV cache fragmentation and synchronous spill events; adds fragmentation_score metric and kernel-aware batching hints. Rollout gated behind feature flags. Improvements: reduced P99 latency and fewer synchronous spill events under mixed workloads.
notes_for_ops: Default behavior unchanged. To enable early canary set KV_SWEEPER_ENABLED=true and EVICTION_WINDOW_MS=200. To rollback set KV_SWEEPER_ENABLED=false or EVICTION_WINDOW_MS=0. Monitor kv.fragmentation_score and kv.soft_spill_rate; alert if soft_spill_rate spikes above configured thresholds.
qa_summary: Unit tests cover scoring and smoothing logic; integration tests exercise canary config and canary harness. Canary run showed stable memory usage and reduced spill frequency. Manual validation performed by SRE on dedicated cluster; no regressions observed on cold-start scenarios with conservative defaults.
